In mathematics, the '''spinor genus''' is a classification of [[quadratic form]]s and lattices over the [[ring of integers]], introduced by [[Martin Eichler]]. It refines the [[Genus of a quadratic form|genus]] but may be coarser than proper equivalence.

==Definitions==
We define two '''Z'''-lattices ''L'' and ''M'' in a [[quadratic space]] ''V'' over '''Q''' to be spinor equivalent if there exists a transformation ''g'' in the proper orthogonal group ''O''<sup>+</sup>(''V'') and for every prime ''p'' there exists a local transformation ''f''<sub>''p''</sub> of ''V''<sub>''p''</sub> of [[spinor norm]] 1 such that ''M'' = ''g'' ''f''<sub>''p''</sub>''L''<sub>''p''</sub>.

A ''spinor genus'' is an equivalence class for this [[equivalence relation]].  Properly equivalent lattices are in the same spinor genus, and lattices in the same spinor genus are in the same genus.  The number of spinor genera in a genus is a power of two, and can be determined effectively.

==Results==
An important result is that for [[indefinite form]]s of dimension at least three, each spinor genus contains exactly one proper equivalence class.
